newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended lower on Wednesday but well off lows, and dealers said they were optimistic after a late recovery erased some losses.
Since the market has closed above 115.50, people expect new highs in coming days, said Jose Ramon Arechederra, trader at ABN Amro in Madrid.
German Bunds were in better shape with the spread to the Spanish 10-year bond widening in the afternoon and closing at 75 basis points versus 73 basis points at the opening.
But dealers said that the underlying trend of the Spanish market remained very positive.
Earlier, the Treasury sold at auction five- and 15-year bonds at falling yields, but dealers said the interest in five-year bonds has not been so high as yesterday's in three-year bonds.
"That could be one reason why in the afternoon the market had fallen a bit more. But I think that was mainly due to a technical movement," said Arechederra.
"The market awaiting news. My guess is that any news, like Spanish CPI would likely push prices higher," another dealer added. May Spanish CPI is scheduled on June 13.
